KADUNA (PSI 9.6): Received formal commendation from President Tinubu for Free CNG Mass Transit (3.2m trips, ₦3.5bn saved); distributed digital devices across 23 LGAs via KADSUBEB; and held federal economic alignment talks with Finance Minister Oyedele.

LAGOS (PSI 9.5): Signed a historic Sister State Agreement with California in Sacramento across tech, ports, and entertainment, while launching the Lagos Clean Energy Schools Innovation Challenge 2026 across secondary education districts.

NIGER (PSI 9.4): Executed emergency crisis management following the death of 37 miners under NSCDC custody: suspended state-wide mining, set up an inquiry committee under Dep Gov Garba, coordinated with IGP Disu/Solid Minerals Ministry, and relaxed the Minna curfew.

ONDO (PSI 9.3): Unveiled the 'Lucky Light Initiative' providing clean solar power to 1,000 small businesses, pledged Dangote Group shares to 500 young entrepreneurs, swore in cabinet members, and announced tertiary student bursary disbursements.

ENUGU (PSI 9.2): Earned presidential spotlight for reducing Enugu-Nsukka transit fares from ₦2,500 to ₦1,500 via CNG buses; inspected Nnamdi Azikiwe Stadium overhauls for the 2026 National Sports Festival; and partnered with SEDC for pilot agro-development.

ABIA (PSI 9.1): Received 2023 SDP candidate Dr. Ngozika Johnson-Chukwunenye into LP; clarified Aba Town Hall direct labor rehab cost at ₦149.2m via former Mayor Uche Wogu; and expanded road reconstruction across Isiala Ngwa South LG.

KATSINA (PSI 9.0): Leading all seven Northwest Governors to a high-level side event at UNGA 81 in New York to present the Northwest Peace, Security and Development Framework 2026–2030 to international financial institutions and investors.

AKWA IBOM (PSI 8.9): Issued appointment letters to 4,000 civil service recruits, approved 2,000 basic education teacher recruitments, commissioned 3.07km Itu-Urua Ekpa Road, and inspected ongoing work at ICC, Ibom Hotel, and ARISE Shopping City.

EBONYI (PSI 8.8): Opened applications for 10,000 slots under the iDICE South-East Skills to Jobs Programme with Del-York/BOI, and commissioned the South-East's first NADDC Automotive Training Centre in Abakaliki alongside Trade Minister Sen. John Owan Enoh.

ZAMFARA (PSI 8.7): Announced recruitment of 800 health workers and posting of 631 nurses, closed non-compliant Tudun Wada Clinic, hosted national Almajiri education reforms, trained maternal 'Big Sisters', and received WHO cholera medicines.

TARABA (PSI 8.6): Sponsored 100 merit-selected first-class/second-upper graduates for fully funded master's degrees in India; called for peace in Mambilla Plateau communities; postponed World Tourism Day; and inspected Wukari FOB construction.

ANAMBRA (PSI 8.5): Commissioned a 3km asphalt road and legislative building built directly by Ekwusigo LGA under Mayor Chimezie Obi; awarded tertiary scholarships and cash grants to 7 student-artisans; and donated ₦5m to local schools.

DELTA (PSI 8.4): Outlined executive measures including a ₦5bn empowerment program for 100,000 households across 500 DCF wards and the 13th-month salary bill, while condemning Effurun political violence and ordering security investigations.

PLATEAU (PSI 8.3): Reaffirmed security protection commitment at the Assemblies of God convention in Jos, while PEPSA convened Jos South stakeholders to unveil a 5-point action plan tackling 53.8% household open defecation.
YOBE (PSI 8.2): YSUTH Damaturu successfully conducted the North-East region's first Total Hip Replacement surgery on a young sickle cell patient suffering from avascular necrosis of the femoral head.

CROSS RIVER (PSI 8.1): Received the remains of late Commissioner for Power Prince Eka Williams at Calabar airport with full state burial commitments, while NIPR commended Lands Commissioner Dr. Erasmus Ekpang for administrative transformation.

KANO (PSI 8.0): Re-constituted the OGP State Steering Committee for open government, while Dep Gov Murtala Garo represented Gov Yusuf at the Tabital Pulaaku summit advocating livestock development and herder-farmer peace.

BENUE (PSI 7.9): Held high-level development financing talks with UNDP Resident Rep Elsie Attafuah at UN House Abuja to establish blended financing, strengthen UNDP's field presence, and align IDP Durable Solutions with SDGs.
OSUN (PSI 7.8): Signed a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) with Critical Minerals Financing Corporation (CMFC) Plc to develop and commercialize state mineral assets under a win-win investment framework.

GOMBE (PSI 7.7): Contained a fire outbreak at Gombe Media Corporation studios without loss of life, while GOSERC held an interactive stakeholder session under the Electricity Act 2023 for state power market regulation.

OGUN (PSI 7.6): Signed the State Education and Skills Trust Fund Bill into law, creating a legal mechanism to provide sustainable funding for formal education, vocational training, and traditional apprenticeship re-engineering.

EKITI (PSI 7.5): Handing over newly acquired operational vehicles to security agency heads at Osuntokun Pavilion, while constructing an 80-bed multipurpose medical facility at EKSUTH Teaching Hospital.
KOGI (PSI 7.4): Declared 3 days of state mourning with flags at half-mast and announced a full State Burial for former Governor Late Alhaji Ibrahim Idris.

SOKOTO (PSI 7.3): Announced state government construction and engineering assessment of the dilapidated Layin Gidan Bello Dan Baba Road in Waziri C Ward during community condolence visits in Sokoto North LG.

ADAMAWA (PSI 7.2): Commissioned the Government House Jumu’ah Mosque in Yola and renovated ADSU International Conference Centre in Mubi, while the Mineral Resources Ministry conducted staff capacity training.
